subject: Unannounced precision fix and requested verification
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rita Chen <rita.chen@acme.ai>, acme-ops@acme.ai
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unannounced precision fix (short notice) — immediate verification requested

Rita / Acme ops team —

We're deploying an unscheduled hotfix right now to address a precision regression we observed in a small subset of quantized model variants that can produce low-confidence hallucinations on tokens following 512+ prompt lengths. The issue surfaced in our telemetry overnight and, after triage, we decided the safest course was a targeted runtime patch (no model weights changed) to correct the attention normalization path.

Impact summary: 
- Affected: ~0.7% of production requests routed to q6x variants when input context > 512 tokens.
- Symptom: repeated low-confidence repetitions and occasionally incorrect numeric outputs.
- Risk: small chance of degraded responses for very long prompts if not patched.

What we're doing now: 
- Deploying hotfix to the serving runtime in your primary region (us-west-2) — rolling, node-by-node.
- Automatic fallback remains enabled to the float32-compatible variant if any node shows anomalous error rates.
- Expected disruption window: 10–40 minutes per node; overall rollout ~2 hours.

Customer action we need from you: 
1) Run the attached verify_script.sh on a small set of representative prompts (script included as attachment).
2) Paste results (pass/fail + trace id) into this thread or upload to the Drive link we shared.

Attachments included: hotfix_patch_notes_v1.pdf (notes & rollback steps) and verify_script.sh (small verification harness).

I'll post progress updates here. If you'd prefer, we can pause the rollout and schedule a maintenance window — but current telemetry suggests patch now will reduce customer risk.

Thanks — apologies for the short notice.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0199

From: Rita Chen <rita.chen@acme.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-ops@acme.ai, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 10:05:24 -0700
Subject: Re: Unannounced precision fix (short notice) — immediate verification requested

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the heads up. A couple quick questions so we can prioritize verifications on our side: 

1) Do you have a concise list of observable symptoms we should check beyond "repetition" and numeric errors (e.g., token-level perplexity spikes, log lines we should look for)?
2) Can you confirm whether this affects embeddings/semantic search or only generation paths? Our ingestion jobs pay 90% to embeddings, so if unaffected we can deprioritize.

We're kicking off the verify script now. If there's a rollback plan, please paste the rollback steps into the thread (we may need to open a quick internal change request).

—Rita
Rita Chen
Head of ML Ops, Acme AI
rita.chen@acme.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Rita Chen <rita.chen@acme.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 13:30:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Unannounced precision fix (short notice) — immediate verification requested

On Tue, Apr 18, 2028 at 10:05 AM Rita Chen <rita.chen@acme.ai> wrote:
> Thanks Jonas — appreciate the heads up. A couple quick questions so we can prioritize verifications on our side: 
> 
> 1) Do you have a concise list of observable symptoms we should check beyond "repetition" and numeric errors (e.g., token-level perplexity spikes, log lines we should look for)?
> 2) Can you confirm whether this affects embeddings/semantic search or only generation paths?

Hi Rita — quick answers: 
- Symptoms to look for: repeated token spans with low log-prob (< -6.5) immediately after context >512 tokens, and generation sequences where the model emits identical 8+ token sequences twice. The verify script checks for both and prints trace ids. Also watch for repeated WARN lines in runtime logs: "attn_norm_outlier" — if you see those at scale, contact us immediately.
- Scope: This is limited to autoregressive generation paths on quantized variants; embeddings pipelines (non-autoregressive encoder-only flows) are not affected. 

Rollback plan (short): 
1) If verification fails or errors increase >1% on your traffic, we will trigger automatic fallback to float32-compatible pool for your account only. 
2) If fallback shows issues, we can roll back the runtime patch entirely; that is a ~15–45 minute operation and will be communicated with impacted windows. Steps are in the attached hotfix_patch_notes_v1.pdf (see section B).

We are collecting verification outputs in the Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.com/s/patch-20280418-jonas-notes (small access grant sent). If you post results here or to the Drive, we'll prioritize your cluster.

I'll monitor and post an update after the first region pass.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
evelyn_hart@redwood.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Rita Chen <rita.chen@acme.ai>, acme-ops@acme.ai
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Apr 2028 16:40:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Unannounced precision fix (short notice) — completion & next steps

Rita / team —

Update: rollout completed in us-west-2 at 16:20 PDT. We observed the expected drop in the "attn_norm_outlier" warnings and the error-rate metric for q6x variants dropped from 0.9% to 0.05% over the first hour post-deploy. Your verify_script.sh results (we saw the Drive upload) show all pass for the sample set you provided — thanks for the quick turnaround.

What we need next: 
- Final confirmation from you that live traffic looks normal over the next 24 hours. If you observe anything, include the trace ids.
- We'll prepare a short postmortem draft and share it tomorrow morning: postmortem-DRAFT.md (attached stub).
- Can we schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10:00 PDT to walk through the root cause and permanent mitigation? If that doesn't work, please suggest a time.

Notes: We proactively scoped the patch to runtime attention normalization changes; we did not touch model weights or quantization tables. The patch is reversible if required; Evelyn's rollback steps are validated.

Apologies again for the short notice. We'll follow up with a full write-up and telemetry dashboards in the morning.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference
